bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary transfers Rs 112.52 crore to over 2.48 lakh flood-hit farmers
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary transfers Rs 112.52 crore to over 2.48 lakh flood-hit farmers ANI | Updated: Oct 14, 2026 16:31 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], October 14 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Wednesday transferred Rs 112.52 crore in agricultural input subsidy to the bank accounts of 2,48,704 farmers whose crops were damaged due to heavy rainfall and floods in the state in August. The amount was transferred through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) under the Agriculture Input Subsidy Scheme at a programme organised by the Agriculture Department at the 'Samvad' hall of the Chief Minister's Secretariat in Patna. Addressing the programme, the Chief Minister said providing assistance to farmers during a crisis remained a priority for the state government. He said the government was committed to providing timely financial relief to farmers affected by natural disasters so that they could resume agricultural activities. According to information presented at the programme, 4,57,616 farmers had applied for the subsidy, of whom 2,48,704 eligible affected farmers received the assistance in the first phase. Choudhary directed officials to launch a special campaign from October 22, after Dussehra, to ensure that farmers whose crops were damaged by floods but who had not yet received assistance were covered. “Ensure that farmers whose crops were damaged by floods also receive the subsidy through a special campaign from October 22. No farmer affected by a disaster should be left deprived of assistance,” the Chief Minister said. Under the Agriculture Input Subsidy Scheme, farmers are provided assistance at the rate of Rs 8,500 per hectare for unirrigated crop areas, Rs 17,000 per hectare for irrigated areas and Rs 22,500 per hectare for perennial crops, according to the state government. The Chief Minister said the assistance would help farmers arrange the resources required to continue cultivation following crop losses. He also acknowledged the work undertaken by the Agriculture Department, Disaster Management Department and other concerned departments in coordinating relief efforts during the floods. Choudhary said the state government was working to protect farmers' interests, strengthen their financial position and improve the agricultural sector. He also referred to the efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar towards addressing farmers' concerns. Deputy Chief Ministers Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Agriculture Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha, Cooperation Minister Ram Kripal Yadav, Disaster Management Minister Ratnesh Sada and senior state officials attended the programme. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: ICAR-MGIFRI, Motihari Organises Training on Natural Farming and PGS-India Certification
bihar_raw_news.content: 12–13 October 2026, Motihari, Bihar ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar, organised a two-day residential training programme on “Natural Farming and PGS-India Certification” during 12–13 October 2026. Sponsored by the Regional Centre for Organic and Natural Farming (RCONF), Bhubaneswar, under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India, the programme aimed to strengthen the technical capacity of agricultural extension personnel, farmers and community-based organisations in natural farming practices and participatory certification. The programme brought together 27 participants, including Subject Matter Specialists from Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), Assistant Technology Managers and Block Technology Managers from the Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA), progressive farmers, JEEViKA representatives and members of Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs). The training was inaugurated by Dr Raghavendra Singh, Director, ICAR-MGIFRI, who emphasised the importance of soil health, efficient resource utilisation, crop diversification and ecological sustainability in building resilient agricultural systems. He highlighted the need for scientific training, practical demonstrations and locally adaptable technologies to promote natural farming, supported by effective extension services and informed management of soil, water and biological resources. The technical sessions covered key principles and practices of natural farming, including crop diversification, residue mulching, non-chemical weed management, soil organic matter management and biological nutrient cycling. Participants were introduced to the integration of field crops, horticulture and livestock for improved resource utilisation and reduced dependence on external inputs. Special emphasis was placed on the preparation and application of farmer-prepared inputs such as Beejamrit, Jeevamrit and Ghanjeevamrit, along with ecological pest management and crop residue utilisation. A major focus of the programme was the Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India) and its role in promoting farmer participation, traceability and certification of eligible production systems. Participants received orientation on certification standards, procedures, peer inspection, documentation requirements, stakeholder responsibilities and web-portal operations. The sessions highlighted the importance of farm records, compliance with prescribed procedures and collective accountability among farmer groups. The programme also introduced participants to soil carbon management, greenhouse gas emission tracking and Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) in sustainable agricultural systems, underscoring the importance of reliable field-level data and scientific assessment in evaluating environmental outcomes. Emphasising institutional convergence, the training highlighted the roles of KVKs, ATMA, FPOs, JEEViKA and other community institutions in promoting natural farming through farmer training, field demonstrations, technical guidance and knowledge dissemination. Participants discussed the importance of strengthening collaboration among research institutions, extension agencies and farmer organisations to support wider adoption of locally appropriate practices and improve access to certification-related guidance. As part of the practical component, participants visited ICAR-MGIFRI’s research facilities, including the institute pond and vermicomposting unit. The exposure visit provided insights into organic waste management, on-farm resource recycling and the integration of complementary farming enterprises. The programme combined technical sessions, interactive discussions, certification orientation and field exposure to strengthen participants’ understanding of natural farming and PGS-India certification. bihar_raw_news.title: CtrlS to invest Rs 10000 crore in Bihar to strengthen digital infrastructure
bihar_raw_news.content: CtrlS Datacenters Ltd. has unveiled a major investment plan to boost Bihar’s digital infrastructure. The company has signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) with the Government of Bihar to invest Rs 10,000 crore to set up a 150 MW hyperscale AI factory in Bodh Gaya, in addition to inaugurating its datacenter in Patna. The company’s Rs 400-crore AI and cloud-ready datacenter in Patna was formally inaugurated in the presence of Hon’ble Chief Minister of Bihar, Shri Samrat Choudhary. The datacenter currently offers an IT load of 12 MW with the potential to expand as per future demand. Located in the Patliputra Industrial Area, Patna, the company’s datacenter facility will support the growing digital infrastructure needs of enterprises, government institutions, hyperscalers and technology businesses in Bihar and Eastern India. The greenfield natural disaster-proof, military-grade security, and energy-efficient datacenter expands CtrlS Datacenters’ footprint in the region, further strengthening Bihar’s digital infrastructure landscape and reinforcing its commitment to supporting the growth of Eastern India’s evolving datacenter ecosystem. Sridhar Pinnapureddy, Founder & CEO of CtrlS Datacenters, said, “We are committed to strengthening Bihar’s digital infrastructure and building a robust IT ecosystem through our future-ready datacenters, designed to serve the evolving needs of hyperscalers, enterprises, and startups. We sincerely appreciate the Government of Bihar for creating a conducive policy environment, fostering an industry-friendly business climate, and providing attractive incentives that have supported our investment in the State.” Pinnapureddy added, “Together with our ecosystem partners, we are bringing significant investments into Bihar while creating new employment opportunities and contributing to the region’s economic growth. The strong market potential and growing demand for digital infrastructure have reinforced our confidence in Bihar. In response to this opportunity, CtrlS Datacenters has established this greenfield datacenter in Patna, further strengthening the State’s digital infrastructure ecosystem.” Looking ahead, CtrlS Datacenters is focused on building a hyper-connected network of datacenters across India and beyond, extending reliable digital infrastructure closer to emerging demand hubs. As part of this strategy, the company plans to establish 20+ Edge datacenters across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities in India over the coming years. As demand grows for localized, low-latency and resilient digital infrastructure, CtrlS is well positioned to accelerate the adoption of Edge datacenters. With a clear roadmap for expansion, the company aims to bring compute and connectivity closer to customers, enabling the next wave of digital services and AI-led applications across India. bihar_raw_news.title: Global Innovation Index 2026 - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: National Current Affairs Prev Next Global Innovation Index 2026 14 Oct 2026 4 min read Why in News? The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) released the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2026 , ranking 139 economies on their innovation performance. India secured the 38th position , remained the top-ranked economy in the Central and Southern Asia region, and continued its 16-year record as an innovation overperformer. Key Points: India’s Performance in GII 2026: Overall Rank: 38th among 139 economies. Regional Position: 1st among 11 economies in Central and Southern Asia. Income Group: 1st among 36 lower-middle-income economies. Innovation Inputs: India ranked 49th , reflecting the conditions and resources supporting innovation. Innovation Outputs: India ranked 25th , indicating stronger performance in translating innovation capabilities into measurable results. Innovation Overperformance: India has been recognised as an innovation overperformer for 16 consecutive years , performing above expectations for its level of development. Top 10 Most Innovative Economies in 2026: 1st: Switzerland 2nd: Sweden 3rd: United States 4th: Republic of Korea 5th: Singapore India’s Key Innovation Strengths: ICT Services Exports: India ranked 1st globally , reflecting its strength in digitally delivered services. Late-Stage Venture Capital Deals: India ranked 4th , indicating its position in financing more mature start-ups. Intangible Asset Intensity: India ranked 13th , highlighting its performance in innovation-related intangible assets. Knowledge and Technology Outputs: India ranked 15th , reflecting its capacity to generate technological and knowledge-based results. Innovation Ecosystem: India's performance demonstrates the role of digital services, entrepreneurship and venture capital in supporting innovation. About the Global Innovation Index (GII): Publisher: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), a specialised agency of the United Nations. Edition: The 2026 report is the 19th edition of the index. First Published: 2007. Coverage: The index evaluates 139 economies using approximately 80 indicators . Purpose: To measure innovation performance and help policymakers understand the strengths and weaknesses of national innovation ecosystems. Framework of the Global Innovation Index: Innovation Input Sub-Index: Measures the conditions that enable innovation through five pillars: Institutions Human capital and research Infrastructure Market sophistication Business sophistication Innovation Output Sub-Index: Measures the results of innovation through two pillars: Knowledge and technology outputs Creative outputs Overall Score: The GII score is calculated using the average of the input and output sub-indices. India’s Global Innovation Clusters: Bengaluru: Ranked 25th among the world's top innovation clusters. Delhi: Ranked 27th . Cluster Assessment: Innovation clusters are identified through the geographical concentration of inventors, scientific authors and venture-capital activity. Significance: These clusters connect research institutions, start-ups, investors and businesses, supporting technological development and commercialisation. Major Global Trends in Innovation: Artificial Intelligence: AI-related businesses are attracting a substantial share of global venture-capital investment. Deep-Science Start-ups: Scientific discoveries are increasingly being translated into scalable commercial technologies. Regional Distribution: Europe continues to account for a substantial share of the leading innovation economies, while Asian economies maintain a strong presence in the top rankings. Innovation Challenge: Economies need to strengthen research, infrastructure, institutions and links between universities and businesses to sustain innovation-led growth Print PDF Print

bihar_raw_news.title: Tokyo promotes sustainable recycling through innovation - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Tokyo promotes sustainable recycling through innovation Updated: 23 hours, 6 min ago Tokyo (Japan), Oct 13 (ANI): “Tokyo Mine” is an initiative to collect used small household appliances containing lithium-ion batteries and for recycling, with the cooperation of Tokyo residents. An AI-powered recycling bin called Bin-e was installed in the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building, and many residents brought lithium-ion batteries from their homes, recovering valuable resources from what is known as an urban mine. Over the past five days, around 50 mobile phones were collected, including other items, total number of collected items rose to more than 10,000. They are transported to a recycling facility, where they are properly processed and recycled. “Tokyo Mine” campaign has ended, but Tokyo Metropolitan Government aims to take leading role in advancing the circular economy. This approach is expected to spread from Tokyo to cities across Asia. This investment surge addresses power and computing constraints, driving interest in integrated energy solutions. ETDatacenters Published On Oct 14, 2026 at 07:41 AM IST Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Highlights US AI data center startups raised $33.5 billion by October 2026. Funding nearly doubled 2025 figures, addressing power and computing constraints. Over 80 per cent of 2026 funds target power supply and computing efficiency. Investment shifts towards integrated power and computing infrastructure solutions. US startups developing technologies for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers raised $33.5 billion in funding by early October 2026, according to a Morgan Stanley report. This figure nearly doubles the total funding raised in 2025. Investors are increasingly supporting technologies that combine energy supply with computing infrastructure, as power availability emerges as a significant challenge for expanding AI data centers . The report highlights that venture funding for this sector accelerated sharply in 2026. The next phase of AI infrastructure development is shifting beyond mere access to computing capacity. It is moving towards integrated systems that coordinate power, computing, networking, and cooling. Power is identified as a key constraint, underscoring the importance of technologies that improve efficiency and secure reliable electricity for data centers. Startups covered in the report have raised over $50 billion since early 2024. This funding spans four areas: expanding power supply, improving computing performance per unit of electricity, integrating power and computing systems, and developing new data center designs and locations. More than 80 per cent of the 2026 funding went to companies focused on expanding power availability and enhancing computing performance relative to electricity consumption. Investment is also broadening from computing technologies into energy infrastructure. In 2026, 73 per cent of funding rounds in the power and computing segments included investors who had previously backed companies in the other segment. This compares to 49 per cent in 2024 and 16 per cent before 2021. The report notes that investors are funding technologies at various development stages. These range from cloud providers deploying computing capacity to advanced nuclear and fusion projects. Companies developing orbital and modular data centers , including Starcloud, Cowboy Space, and Armada, collectively raised nearly $1 billion in 2026. However, the report cautioned that raising capital alone would not be sufficient for commercial viability. It stated that validation should shift from capital raised to capacity deployed. Commercial agreements, regulatory approvals, initial deployments, and evidence of competitive operating costs would become more crucial. The report also pointed out risks from licensing requirements, construction delays, grid connections, and long procurement cycles. bihar_raw_news.content: Adyar-Lighthouse corridor among five projects included in feasibility study Photo | Express Tamil Nadu Rs 98 lakh allotted to prepare DPR for 5 key infra projects State Highways officials said the elevated corridor may run from Pattinapakkam via Loop Road to the Adyar landing near Malar Hospital. B Anbuselvan Updated: 14th Oct, 2026 at 7:24 AM CHENNAI: The state highways has issued a G.O. allocating Rs 98 lakh to prepare detailed project reports (DPRs) for five infrastructure projects in Chennai, including an elevated corridor from the Lighthouse to Adyar near Malar Hospital. The other projects include extending one arm of the Vyasarpadi road overbridge (ROB) towards Madhavaram, widening the ROB at Basin Bridge to ease traffic congestion in North Chennai, widening the bridge across the Cooum river at Koyambedu on the Thirumangalam-Koyambedu stretch of Jawaharlal Nehru Road (Inner Ring Road), and constructing a link road between Rajiv Gandhi Salai and East Coast Road. While four projects were allocated Rs 20 lakh each, one was given Rs 18 lakh, revealed the recent G.O. issued by the department. Official sources in the state highways said the elevated corridor is likely to start from Pattinapakkam, via the Loop Road, and connect to the Adyar landing near Malar Hospital. “The plan is to decongest Santhome High Road, which witnesses heavy traffic during peak hours. Other design parameters, including the length and width of the corridor, will be finalised during the preparation of the DPR,” an official said. Add as a preferred source on Google The department plans to extend one arm of the 1,720-metre-long Y-shaped Vyasarpadi ROB towards Madhavaram. The bridge, which begins near Basin Bridge, branches into two arms - one connecting Moolakadai, Madhavaram and Puzhal and the other leading to Sathyamurthy Nagar Main Road near Kalyanapuram, catering to local traffic. The narrow ROB at Basin Bridge junction, an important link connecting Korukkupet, Vyasarpadi and Purasawalkam, is also set to be widened. The department has also proposed widening the existing six-lane bridge across the Cooum river at Koyambedu, which witnesses heavy congestion during peak hours. A link road connecting Rajiv Gandhi Salai and ECR is proposed, with its alignment and location to be identified during the preparation of the DPR. national_raw_news.title: 38 mins ago | National 38 EAM S Jaishankar says world is moving towards new international order, with wide range of countri...
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr. Jaishankar today said that consensus, mutual understanding and self-interest would play a key role on the enforcement of rules agreed upon by middle powers. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Dr. Jaishankar emphasized that the era of a country dictating terms to others through threats is over. He noted that the world is moving towards a new international order, with a wider range of countries playing a greater role in global affairs. He added the current transition should not be seen as a shift from order to disorder but as the evolution of a different kind of order. Dr. S Jaishankar also said that India does not identify itself as a middle power, but rather as a power in the middle. The External Affairs Minister emphasized that India is the world’s most populous country with a GDP of around four trillion dollars and has significant growth potential. He added that hence the term ‘middle power’ does not adequately reflect India’s position and ambitions. He further noted that middle powers would now increasingly define their own interests, formulate independent policies and reach agreements with one another. He said this would enable middle powers to play a more active role in shaping the emerging international order.

national_raw_news.content: Union Electronics and Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said that trust and cybersecurity are becoming increasingly important in the global semiconductor value chain, alongside cost considerations. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi today Mr Vaishnaw said that India aims to position itself as a trusted partner in semiconductor design, manufacturing and testing of finished products. The Minister emphasised that developing a complete ecosystem is essential for sustainable manufacturing. Citing the mobile phone industry, Mr. Vaishnaw said India initially focused on assembly before expanding into module and component manufacturing. He added that the country is now manufacturing components to meet domestic demand and has also started exporting them. The Minister said India is following a similar approach to develop its semiconductor, railway and defence manufacturing ecosystems Mr Vaishnaw has said that India is strengthening its economy. He said that India’s public debt-to-GDP ratio has declined from 61% to 55% over the past five years. The Minister emphasised that the country aims to build resilience across the financial, economic and technological sectors. Mr. Vaishnaw said that the government is working to strengthen the domestic economy and reduce its vulnerability to global uncertainties to ensure sustained growth even during turbulent times.
